records.learner: The panels live in a private bucket, and storage rules block direct reads for every user, so the only way to an image is through our API route. That route checks the session and whether this user has access to that chapter, and if yes, the server signs the file path with a 120-second expiry and returns it with Cache-Control: no-store. The reader asks for links panel by panel as you scroll, and since all the links share one global two-minute timer that rotates them, a scraper only ever holds a few that die quickly.
records.planted_point: The misconception is treating the 120-second expiry as one global timer that rotates all links together; the correct version is that each signed URL expires 120 seconds after it is signed, independently.
records.tutor: Feedback: You said all the links share one global timer; each link expires 120 seconds after it is signed. You mentioned that the API checks access, but how does the database ensure that even if the API is bypassed, data remains secure?

records.learner: Sure, it's five weekly milestones plus a QA week, and every Wednesday the code is on your GitHub and on Vercel staging. Week one is the foundation: the full schema in Supabase, Row Level Security on every table, the 45/55 split, and the private buckets. Then week four is payments with the Centrobill iframe and postback, the paywall at chapter four, and the 18-plus gate, and week five is payouts and revenue, with the Paxum ledger, the ad slots and the print-on-demand webhooks, and week six is only testing and polish, with sign-off on December 24th.

records.learner: I use pg_cron inside Supabase, and it calls one SQL function that does everything in a single transaction: copy the week's winners to the archive table, then set the counters to zero. If something fails, nothing changes. And a unique key on the week makes a repeated run harmless, so if it runs twice by mistake the second run does nothing. Actually I would prefer to store votes per week, because then the reset never deletes anything.
